title: Comparing Scribe v3 Pricing and Team Seat Costs in 2026
summary: Scribe v3 pricing structures vary by user count and required administrative controls. Use this breakdown to select the tier that fits your team size.
body_markdown:
## Scribe v3 Pricing Plans and Feature Tiers


> **The leap from $35 to $85 occurs the moment a single person needs to collaborate with a colleague** , which means your operational costs more than double the instant you begin working as a team.


### Scribe Free plan features for individuals


When you need to test the capture engine on web-based applications, the Free plan acts as a sandbox. Because this tier restricts captures to browser extensions and mobile apps, you can't document workflows involving desktop-native software like Excel or legacy ERP systems.


Documentation generated here remains hosted on the vendor's servers with mandatory branding. The lack of bulk export options ensures that moving a large library of guides into a different knowledge base requires manual effort for every single document.


### Pro Personal vs. Pro Team tiers


The Pro tiers introduce the ability to capture desktop applications, but they bifurcate your experience based on the need for collaboration. Pro Personal is for the lone wolf who needs to export clean, unbranded guides to PDF or Word but doesn't require a shared workspace.


By moving to the Pro Team tier, you trigger a seat minimum. You must pay for a set number of licenses even if only two people are actively creating content.


To manage these costs, you'll often look toward automation via Activepieces to sync documentation across platforms without manually adding every viewer as a paid seat.


Because the platform bills 1 credit per flow run regardless of how many steps are involved, a complex ten-step synchronization costs exactly the same as a basic two-step transfer.


This flat-rate execution model allows teams to build granular, reliable documentation flows without the per-task tax that often punishes detailed automation.

### Enterprise requirements for large scale


Regulated industries or large-scale deployments require the security infrastructure provided by Enterprise plans. Single Sign-On (SSO) and SOC2 compliance live behind this custom-priced gate.


Redacted captures are also introduced at this tier, which automatically mask sensitive data like credit card numbers during the recording process. This ensures private information never reaches the cloud.


For teams scaling across hundreds of users, this is the only way to ensure that shadow documentation doesn't lead to a data breach, which means security protocols remain consistent as the organization grows.
